text: Every time a flow runs, ServiceNow creates an execution record for that specific run. You can reach it two ways: open the flow in Flow Designer and check its Runs, its execution history, or go through the platform's central execution log that tracks every flow and subflow context across the instance. Either path lands on the same underlying data.

Open a specific run and you see every action listed in the order it executed, each with its own status: completed, failed, cancelled, or waiting. For completed actions, you can see exactly how long each step took, which helps you find a slow step instead of assuming the whole flow is slow. You can also inspect the actual input and output values for that action.

When a flow misbehaves, don't reason it out from the design canvas alone. Open the run, walk the steps in execution order, and inspect what a data pill actually resolved to at that moment, for that specific record. If a branch went the wrong way, the log shows you the real value it evaluated, not what you assumed.

Not every run that hasn't finished has failed. A run can be legitimately paused, waiting on something external, most commonly an unanswered approval or an unmet wait condition. The log shows a paused run sitting at an action with a waiting status and no error.

A failed run looks different: it shows a specific action with an error status and an error message describing exactly what went wrong, such as an unmapped required input or a failed REST call. Confusing a paused flow for a broken one, or the reverse, is the most common mistake this log exists to prevent.

This log is Flow Designer's purpose-built sibling to the System Log: instead of scanning instance-wide events, you go straight to the one record describing exactly the run you care about. Next, the real failure categories this log helps you diagnose.
